info.title: Merchant API
info.description: One API for taking payments on every method and channel your account is set up for. Start with the [Overview](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/overview/) and the [Quickstart](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/quickstart/), then see [Authentication](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/authentication/), [Test mode and test values](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/test-mode/), [Testing your integration](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/testing-your-integration/) and the API basics ([Errors](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/errors/), [Idempotency](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/idempotency/), [Pagination](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/pagination/) and [Versioning](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/versioning/)); everything here is `/v1`.

tags.name: Payment intents
tags.description: One payment to take, whatever the method; [Payment intents](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/payment-intents/) explains its lifecycle and the three ways a customer pays.

tags.name: Payment methods
tags.description: The methods your account can take payments with, one per method and channel, and whether each can take a payment now; [Payment intents](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/payment-intents/) explains how a customer pays by one.

tags.name: Test helpers
tags.description: Calls that stand in for what a customer does, in test mode only; [Testing your integration](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/testing-your-integration/) explains every outcome.

tags.name: Refunds
tags.description: Money returned to a customer from a payment that succeeded, in full or in part; [Refunds](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/refunds/) explains which payments can be refunded and what a refund goes through.

tags.name: Disputes
tags.description: A customer's challenge to one of your card payments, raised through their bank; [Disputes](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/disputes/) explains what it costs, how it goes and how to respond.

tags.name: Webhook endpoints
tags.description: HTTPS addresses we send events to as they happen; [Webhooks](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/webhooks/) explains how to create one, verify a delivery and what happens when it fails.

tags.name: Event types
tags.description: What each event we deliver carries, which [Webhooks](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/webhooks/#event-types) lists with its object as of the event.

tags.name: Access tokens
tags.description: Short-lived tokens your server exchanges its client credentials for; see [Authentication](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/authentication/).

post.description:
Starts a payment of `amount` in `currency`. Name the method now in
`payment_method_data[type]`, and the intent is `requires_confirmation` with its method and
price fixed. Leave it out, and the intent is `requires_action` with the methods it can be paid
by in `payment_method_types`, and `next_action.redirect_to_url`: send your customer to its
`url`, our hosted checkout page, or choose a method yourself when you confirm. Without a
method, a `return_url` is where our hosted checkout page sends the customer back to, a
`cancel_url` where it sends one who cancels, and a `customer_email` where it offers to send
the receipt.

With `checkout_mode` `embedded`, the intent is paid in embedded checkout, on your own page,
instead: its `next_action` is `mount_embedded_checkout`, with the client token your page
mounts it with. A `return_url` is then where the customer is sent after paying by card, and a
`cancel_url` is refused. See [Embedded checkout](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/embedded-checkout/).

With `confirm: true`, the intent is created and confirmed in one call, and comes back
`requires_action` with `next_action`. Name the method, and a `return_url` for a card.

`payment_method`, the id of a saved payment method, is not supported yet and is refused with
`validation_failure`.

amount.description: In the currency's minor unit, at most 18 digits.

currency.description: A three-letter ISO 4217 code, in either case.

payment_method_types.description:
The methods this intent may be paid by. Leave it out to allow any your account
can take. A method in `payment_method_data[type]` must be one of them.

description.description: Your own text, such as an order number. Never shown to the customer.

confirm.description:
`true` creates and confirms the intent in one call. `payment_method_data[type]` is
then required.

201.description:
The intent: `requires_action` with `next_action.redirect_to_url` to our hosted checkout
page when created without a method, or `next_action.mount_embedded_checkout` with
`checkout_mode` `embedded`; `requires_confirmation` with a method; or `requires_action`
with `next_action` when created with `confirm: true`.

get.description: Your payment intents in this key's mode, oldest first.

200.description: A page of intents.
The intent.

post.description:
Starts an attempt at the payment, and the customer acts next: the intent moves to
`requires_action` and `next_action` says what to show them. An intent without a method takes
one here in `payment_method_data[type]`, from its `payment_method_types`. An intent with its
method may name it again or leave it out; naming another is a `conflict`, since its price is
fixed with it — except after a failed attempt, when the customer may pay another way.

Confirm an intent that is `requires_payment_method` or `requires_confirmation`: its first
attempt, or another after one failed. An intent created without a method and waiting at our
hosted checkout page is `requires_action`, and confirming it with a method starts its first
attempt all the same. Confirming one already `requires_action` after a confirmation answers it
unchanged, and however often it is confirmed, the customer is given one code or page per
attempt. Any other status is a `conflict`.

200.description: The intent, in `requires_action`.

post.description:
Cancels an intent the customer has not paid: one that is `requires_payment_method`,
`requires_confirmation` or `requires_action`. Canceling one already `canceled` answers it
unchanged. Once it is `processing` or `succeeded`, or while a confirm is still reaching the
payment method, it cannot be canceled: that is a `conflict`.

cancellation_reason.description: Why you are canceling it. Optional.

200.description: The intent, in `canceled`, with `canceled_at` and `cancellation_reason`.

post.description:
Gives a test-mode payment the outcome you choose, now, as if your customer had paid it, or
failed to. No customer pays a simulated QR code or a test cash reference, and no bank answers a
simulated card, so this is how a test payment moves on from `requires_action`. It works with a test key only: a live
key is refused with `test_mode_only`, and a live intent is never reached. See [Testing your
integration](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/testing-your-integration/).

The intent must have a payment with the customer: [confirmed](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/reference/operations/confirmpaymentintent/),
or, for an intent created without a method, with the method chosen on our checkout page.
Outcomes are for the intent's method:

| `outcome` | Method | The intent then |
|---|---|---|
| `paid` | `qrph` | `succeeded`, with `amount_received` equal to `amount`. A code already past its time is `expired` instead. |
| `expired` | `qrph` | `requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` `payment_intent_payment_attempt_expired`. The code can no longer be paid; confirm again for a new one. |
| `paid` | `cash` | `succeeded` through `processing`, as when the customer pays the exact amount at a cash collection location. A reference already past its time is `expired` instead. |
| `expired` | `cash` | `requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` `payment_intent_payment_attempt_expired`. The reference can no longer be paid; confirm again for a new one. |
| `approved` | `card` | `succeeded`. A card payment of `40400` is then charged back: see [Test mode and test values](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/test-mode/). |
| `three_d_secure_passed` | `card` | `succeeded`, as after the customer's bank has authenticated them. |
| `declined` | `card` | `requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` `card_declined`. A `decline_reason` adds a `decline_code` to it (test mode only). |
| `three_d_secure_failed` | `card` | `requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` `payment_intent_authentication_failure`. |
| `abandoned` | `card` | `requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` `payment_intent_payment_attempt_failed`: the customer left without paying. |

The intent and its events are those of a real payment: `payment_intent.succeeded` or
`payment_intent.payment_failed` is sent, and a failed card payment can be confirmed again. An
intent already settled, whether paid, canceled, or its attempt failed or expired, is answered
as it is, and nothing changes: asking again, for the same outcome or another, is safe. An
outcome that is not one of the intent's method is refused with `validation_failure`
whatever the intent's state.

`Idempotency-Key` is required, as on every write on an intent.

200.description: The intent as it then is.

400.description:
`validation_failure` with `invalid_parameter`: `param` is `outcome` when it is missing,
not an outcome, or not one for the intent's method; `decline_reason` when it is not
`insufficient_funds`, `do_not_honor` or `expired_card`, or is sent with an outcome other
than `declined`; `Idempotency-Key` when the header is missing.

error.message: One of paid, expired for a qrph payment.

403.description:
`authorization_failure` with `test_mode_only`: a live key was used. Nothing is simulated
in live mode, and a live intent is not reachable even with a test key. Also
`merchant_mismatch`, as on every call.

error.message: Test helpers take a test key: no outcome is simulated in live mode.

409.description:
`conflict` with `intent_state`: the intent has no payment with the customer to give an
outcome to. It is not confirmed yet, it is `requires_action` at our checkout page with no
method chosen, or it is `processing`. Confirm it, or have the customer choose a method, and
ask again. `idempotency_key_reused` and `idempotency_key_in_use` as on every write.

get.description: Your enabled methods, ordered by method then channel.

200.description: A page of payment methods.
The payment method.

post.description:
Returns all or part of a succeeded card payment, or the whole of a succeeded cash payment (see [Accepting
cash](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/accepting-cash/): that refund stays `processing` until your operator records it paid out). Leave `amount` out to refund what remains.
The payment intent stays `succeeded`; the refund is its own object. A payment can be refunded
more than once, until all of it has been. Fees are not returned by a refund. In test mode, a
card payment that was simulated paid is refunded at once: the refund comes back `succeeded`
and nothing is returned.

The refund comes back `succeeded`, `processing` while it is still on its way (a
`refund.succeeded` or `refund.failed` event follows), or `failed` with a `failure_reason`.
Every refund made sends `refund.created`, then `refund.updated` as it goes on its way, then
`refund.succeeded` or `refund.failed`.

Refusals, each with nothing refunded. The first three are refused before any refund is made.
The last two, and `refund_not_possible` when the card provider says so, are refused once the
card provider has answered: the refund is kept, `failed` with the same `failure_reason`, and
is listed and sent as `refund.failed` like any other.

| `type` | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| `invariant_violation` | `amount_exceeds_refundable` | More than the payment has left to refund. |
| `policy_rejection` | `refund_not_possible` | The payment intent has not succeeded, was not paid by card or cash, or can no longer be refunded. |
| `policy_rejection` | `refund_not_supported_by_provider` | The payment was made by QR, and its provider can't refund it. Refund the customer another way, such as in cash, and keep a record of it. |
| `policy_rejection` | `refund_not_yet_available` | Part of a card payment cannot be refunded on the day it was made. Refund all of it the same day, or part of it from the next day. |
| `policy_rejection` | `refunds_not_enabled` | Refunds are not enabled for your account with its card provider. Ask your platform operator to have them enabled. |

amount.description: In the currency's smallest unit. Leave it out to refund what remains.

get.description: Your refunds in this key's mode, oldest first.

200.description: The refund.

get.description:
Your disputes in this key's mode, oldest first. Filter by the payment disputed with
`payment_intent`, and by `status`. A `status` that is not one of the five is refused with
`validation_failure` and `param` `status`.

200.description: A page of disputes.

get.description: Another merchant's dispute, or one in the other mode, is `not_found`.

200.description: The dispute.

post.description:
The endpoint's signing `secret` is returned on this response only: store it where your
receiver can read it. The URL must be `https://` and resolve only to public addresses;
addresses on private networks are refused with `validation_failure` on `url`.

`enabled_events` takes the event types that are sent today, those listed in
[Webhooks](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/webhooks/#event-types) without a Pending badge. A Pending type is refused with `validation_failure` until it ships, so a
subscription is never accepted and then sent nothing. `["*"]` subscribes to every type,
including those added later; `*` stands alone and is refused beside named types.

get.description: Your endpoints in this key's mode.

200.description: A page of endpoints.

post.description:
Changes where the endpoint is, which events it is sent, or whether it is sent anything: set
`status` to `enabled` to turn a disabled endpoint back on. Leave out what stays. Deliveries
that failed while it was disabled stay failed.

enabled_events.description: The types to send, or `["*"]` for every type, including those added later.

200.description: The endpoint.

post.description: Stops sending to the endpoint. Deliveries still waiting to be tried fail when they are.

200.description: The endpoint, disabled.

post.description:
Issues a new signing secret, returned on this response only. For 24 hours deliveries carry a
signature made with each, so your receiver can switch over without dropping an event.

200.description: The endpoint, with its new secret.

post.description:
Exchanges your client ID and secret for an Access Token (the OAuth 2.0 client credentials
grant, RFC 6749). Send the client ID and secret in a Basic `Authorization` header, or as
`client_id` and `client_secret` in the body, not both, and each parameter once. The token
lasts 15 minutes; any
standard OAuth client library can call this and fetch a new token as each expires.

Errors follow RFC 6749, not the `/v1` envelope. Every client ID and secret that proves
nothing — an unknown client, a wrong secret, a revoked key — gets the same `invalid_client`.
Token requests are rate limited per client ID and per address.

client_id.description: With `client_secret`, instead of a Basic header.

client_secret.description: With `client_id`, instead of a Basic header.

schema.description: The same parameters as a JSON object, for a client that sends JSON.

200.description: The token. Every answer here is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`.

400.description: `invalid_request` (no `grant_type`, or the client authenticated both ways), or `unsupported_grant_type` (anything but `client_credentials`).

401.description: `invalid_client`: the client ID or secret is not valid. Sent with a `WWW-Authenticate: Basic` header.

429.description: `rate_limited`: too many token requests. Try again shortly.

post.description:
A payment intent was created. Its `next_action` is `null` even when it was created without a
method: read the intent for its hosted checkout link, or its embedded checkout client token.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description:
A payment intent waits for the customer: `next_action` says what they are to do. Sent when an
intent is confirmed, and when one is created without a method to wait at our hosted checkout
page or in embedded checkout. For that one, `next_action` is `null`: read the intent for its
hosted checkout link, or its embedded checkout client token.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: The customer acted and the outcome is not known yet.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: The payment succeeded.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description:
An attempt to pay failed: declined, failed, not paid in time, or left by the customer. The
intent is back in
`requires_payment_method`, with `last_payment_error` saying why, and waits for another
confirmation.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: The payment intent was canceled.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: A refund was created.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: A refund changed: it is on its way.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: A refund reached the customer.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description: A refund could not be made. `failure_reason` says why.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description:
A customer disputed one of your card payments through their bank: a chargeback was raised
and its dispute opened, `open`. Sent once per dispute, however often the card network reports
the same case. The disputed amount, `chargeback_cost` and `admin_fee` are taken from the funds
due to you from now. `evidence_due_date` says by when to respond: see [Disputes](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/disputes/).

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

object.evidence_request: Proof of delivery signed by the customer, and the order's invoice.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

post.description:
A dispute was decided, and `closed` says when. Its `status` is final:

- `won`: the case was decided for you, or the network reversed the chargeback. The disputed
  amount is returned to you, and so is the chargeback cost if the card provider returned
  it: `cost_returned` says how much.
- `lost`: the case was decided for the customer. Nothing is returned.
- `accepted`: you, or the operations team, accepted the chargeback. Nothing is returned.

Nothing is sent for a dispute after this.

object.evidence_request: Proof of delivery signed by the customer, and the order's invoice.

200.description: Received. Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds.

AccessToken.description:
An Access Token from `POST /oauth/token`, `at_test_...` or `at_live_...`, as a Bearer token.
It lasts 15 minutes. The client secret is refused here.

ClientSecret.description:
Your client ID and client secret, `ci_test_...` and `sk_test_...` in test mode, sent to the
token endpoint only.

WebhookEndpointCreateUnavailable.description: `dependency_failure` with `service_unavailable`: something on our side did not answer, or failed part-way. Whether the endpoint was created is not known, and its signing secret is shown only in the answer you did not get. This call takes no `Idempotency-Key`, so sending it again makes a second endpoint if the first was made. List your endpoints first with [List webhook endpoints](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/reference/operations/listwebhookendpoints/): if the endpoint is there, do not create another; [rotate its secret](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/reference/operations/rotatewebhookendpointsecret/) to get a secret you can read, or disable it. If it is not, create it again.

WebhookEndpointChangeUnavailable.description: `dependency_failure` with `service_unavailable`: something on our side did not answer, or failed part-way. Whether the change was made is not known. This call takes no `Idempotency-Key` and needs none: send the same request again, and the endpoint ends up as the first call would have left it, however many times it is sent. Read the endpoint to see how it stands.

WebhookEndpointSecretUnavailable.description: `dependency_failure` with `service_unavailable`: something on our side did not answer, or failed part-way. Whether the secret was rotated is not known, and a new secret is shown only in the answer you did not get. This call takes no `Idempotency-Key`: send it again, and it rotates again, so use the secret in the answer you receive. A secret the unanswered call made, or the one before it, keeps signing for 24 hours and then stops.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: `resource_missing` for an id this key cannot see, `route_missing` for a path that does not exist.

AuthorizationFailure.description: `authorization_failure` with `merchant_mismatch`: a `Merchant-Id` header, query parameter or body field names a merchant or tenant other than the key's.

AuthenticationFailure.description: `authentication_failure`: `access_token_required` when no token was sent, `invalid_access_token` when it is not valid, has expired, or is a client secret. Sent with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header, which adds `error="invalid_token"` when a token was sent.

DependencyFailure.description: `dependency_failure` with `service_unavailable`: something on our side, or a payment network behind it, did not answer. This call only reads, so nothing was changed; retry.

ValidationFailure.description: `validation_failure`: `invalid_parameter` for a parameter missing or not valid, named in `param`; `invalid_json` for a body that is not JSON; `unsupported_media_type` for a body that is not sent as JSON; `not_acceptable` when the request will not accept JSON; `method_not_allowed` for an HTTP method the path does not take.

error.message: A whole number of minor units, from 1 to 999999999999999999.

KeyedWriteUnavailable.description: `dependency_failure` with `service_unavailable`: something on our side, or a payment network behind it, did not answer, or failed part-way. Whether the call took effect is not known, so do not assume it did not. Retry the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key`, and never make a new key for the retry: if the first call took effect, you are answered with its result (the payment intent or refund it made, or the intent as it now is) and nothing is done a second time. A retry refused with `conflict` and `intent_state` means the intent is no longer in a state that allows the call: the first call may have taken effect, or the customer may have acted since. Read the intent. If the failure came while the answer was being stored, the key is held for five minutes and a retry in that time answers `409` with `idempotency_key_in_use`: retry shortly. See [When a write answers 503](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/idempotency/#when-a-write-answers-503).

PolicyRejection.description: `policy_rejection`: your account may not do this now, for the reason in `code`.

Conflict.description: `conflict`: `intent_state` when the intent is not in a state that allows this; `idempotency_key_reused` when the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `timeout_or_in_progress` with `idempotency_key_in_use` while a request with the same key is still running, or with `refund_in_progress` for a refund while another refund of the same payment is still being processed.

PaymentRefused.description:
`policy_rejection`: this payment cannot be taken now. `code` says why:

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `account_inactive` | Your account is not active. |
| `not_permitted_for_account` | Your account may not use this method yet. |
| `method_not_enabled` | The method is not enabled for your account. |
| `method_not_set_up` | The method is enabled but its setup is not finished. |
| `method_suspended` | The method is suspended for your account. |
| `pricing_unavailable` | No price is set for this method and amount. |
| `payment_method_unavailable` | The method cannot take this payment on this channel yet. |
| `no_payment_method_available` | None of your methods can take this payment now. |
| `test_mode_unavailable` | Confirming only: this method cannot be simulated in test mode. |
| `limit_exceeded` | Confirming only: this payment would take your account past its limit. |
| `restricted` | Confirming only: payments are restricted for your account, store or terminal at the moment. |
| `risk_declined` | Confirming only: this payment was declined by a risk check. |
| `not_available` | Unavailable for another reason. |

error.message: This payment method is suspended for your account.

IntentEmbedded.summary: Created without a method, for embedded checkout

cash_display_reference.instructions: Give this reference to the cashier at a cash collection location and pay the exact amount in cash.

IntentSimulatedPaid.summary: A QR Ph payment simulated paid

IntentSimulatedDeclined.summary: A card payment simulated declined for insufficient funds

DisputeUnderReview.summary: Under review, with evidence asked for

value.evidence_request: Proof of delivery signed by the customer, and the order's invoice.
Proof of delivery signed by the customer, and the order's invoice.

amount_received.description: The amount paid: `amount` once `succeeded`, and `0` until then.

payment_method_types.description:
The chosen method, such as `[qrph]`, once there is one. Until then, the methods that can
take this payment now: confirm with one. In an event for an intent with no method, the
methods you allowed at creation, or `null` if you allowed any.

channel.description:
Where the payment is taken: `ecommerce` for every intent your server creates. Payments
taken on terminals will say `pos` (Pending).

next_action.description:
What the customer is to do, while the intent is `requires_action`. `null` otherwise. For
an intent created without a method, `redirect_to_url` to our hosted checkout page while
its checkout link is open, or, with `checkout_mode` `embedded`, `mount_embedded_checkout`
while its checkout session is open; either until the customer starts a payment there,
when it is that payment's own step. An event never carries the link or the client
token: read the intent for them.

last_payment_error.description: Why the last attempt failed. `null` again once another attempt starts.

cancellation_reason.description: The reason given when it was canceled, if any.

canceled_at.description: When it was canceled, as a Unix timestamp.

metadata.description: The `metadata` you gave it. `{}` if none.

created.description: When it was created, as a Unix timestamp.

data.description: The QR payload. Render it as a QR code for the customer to scan with their banking app.

expires_at.description: When the code stops being payable, as a Unix timestamp.

reference.description: The payment reference, unique to this attempt. Give it to the customer to pay at a cash collection location.

amount.description: The exact amount to pay, in the currency's minor unit.

expires_at.description: When the reference stops being payable, as a Unix timestamp. After it the attempt fails as expired.

instructions.description: Words to show the customer. May be reworded, so never branch on it.

url.description:
The payment page: a card's, or our hosted checkout page for an intent created without
a method. Send the customer there.

return_url.description:
Where the customer comes back to, or null when you gave none: your `return_url`, or our hosted checkout page when
the customer chose card there, which then sends them on to yours. For the hosted
checkout page itself, the `return_url` you gave on create.

MountEmbeddedCheckout.description:
An intent created with `checkout_mode` `embedded`, waiting for the customer in embedded
checkout on your page. See [Embedded checkout](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/embedded-checkout/).

client_token.description:
What your page mounts embedded checkout with, beside your publishable key, from one of
your registered origins. The same on every read while it is here. It opens this one
payment's checkout: give it only to the customer paying.

expires_at.description: When the checkout session ends, as a Unix timestamp. After it, the client token opens nothing.

CheckoutMode.description:
Where the customer pays an intent created without a method: `hosted`, on our hosted checkout
page, which `next_action.redirect_to_url` links to; or `embedded`, in embedded checkout on
your own page, which `next_action.mount_embedded_checkout` gives the client token for. Only
on create, and only with no payment method and without `confirm`; anywhere else, or any
other value, is refused with `param` `checkout_mode`. With `embedded`, a `cancel_url` is
refused.

code.description:
`card_declined`: the card was declined. `expired_card`: the card has expired (test mode
only today). `payment_intent_authentication_failure`: the customer did not complete the
card's authentication. `payment_intent_payment_attempt_failed`: the attempt failed, or the
customer left without paying. `payment_intent_payment_attempt_expired`: the customer did
not pay in time.

decline_code.description:
Why the card was declined, when the decline names a reason. **Test mode only today:** it
appears when you simulate a decline with a `decline_reason` (see [Simulate a payment's
outcome](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/reference/operations/simulatepaymentintent/)), and a live decline does not carry it yet, so
never depend on it there.

message.description: Words you can show the customer. May be reworded, so never branch on it.

outcome.description:
`paid` or `expired` for a QR Ph or cash payment; `approved`, `declined`,
`three_d_secure_passed`, `three_d_secure_failed` or `abandoned` for a card payment.

decline_reason.description:
With `declined` only: the reason the decline names, which comes back as
`last_payment_error.decline_code`. Leave it out, or send `null`, for a plain decline.

PaymentMethodData.description:
The method to pay with. Its price is fixed with it until an attempt fails. A method that is
missing or not valid is
refused with `validation_failure` and `param` `payment_method_data[type]`.

type.description: A payment method type, such as `qrph`, `card` or `cash`.

Metadata.description:
Your own key-value pairs, returned as given and carried in webhooks: up to 50 keys of up to
40 characters without square brackets, each with a text value of up to 500 characters.

RiskSignals.description:
What you know of the customer paying, for the platform's risk checks. Each is optional; send
what you have. The email is hashed before it is checked and is never stored. Send these with
the confirmation: on create only with `confirm: true`.

ip_address.description: The customer's IP address, IPv4 or IPv6, as your server saw it.

device_id.description: Your identifier for the customer's device or browser session.

ReturnUrl.description:
Where the customer comes back to after a payment page, such as a card's. Required to confirm
a card payment; one given here replaces an earlier one. `https` in live mode, `http` or
`https` in test mode. On create, only with `confirm: true` — or with no payment method, when
it is where our hosted checkout page sends the customer back to once they are done, or, with
`checkout_mode` `embedded`, where our return page sends them after paying by card; embedded
checkout offers card only when the intent has one.

The customer comes back with `payment_intent=<id>` added to it, and from the hosted checkout
page with `checkout_session=<id>` too, never a status. Coming back proves nothing: retrieve
the intent, or wait for its webhook, to know how it went.

CancelUrl.description:
Where our hosted checkout page sends a customer who cancels. Only on create, and only with no
payment method and without `confirm`; refused with `checkout_mode` `embedded`, where a
customer who cancels stays on your page. `https` in live mode, `http` or `https` in test mode, as
for `return_url`. Without one, a customer who cancels goes to your `return_url`.

The customer comes back with `payment_intent=<id>` and `checkout_session=<id>` added to it,
never a status. It is not shown on the intent.

CustomerEmail.description:
Your customer's email, if you have it: our hosted checkout page, or embedded checkout, fills
its optional receipt field with it, and the customer can change or clear it. Once the payment succeeds, one
receipt is sent to the address the customer leaves there. Only on create, and only with no
payment method and without `confirm`; anything that is not an email address is refused
with `param` `customer_email`.

It is used for the receipt and, hashed, for our risk checks. It is not shown on the intent,
nor sent in any event or webhook.

available.description: Whether it can take a payment now.

unavailable_reason.description: Why it cannot, when `available` is false.

status.description:
`created` for the moment it is made, `processing` while it is on its way, then
`succeeded` or `failed`. `awaiting_approval` while the platform's risk team looks at it
before it is sent: it then goes on, or fails as `risk_declined`. Nothing is refunded while
it waits, and the amount stays held against what the payment has left to refund.

failure_reason.description: Why it failed, when it did.

Dispute.description:
A customer's challenge to one of your card payments, as you see it. The payment itself never
changes: it stays `succeeded`, and the dispute is its own object.

amount.description:
The amount disputed, in the currency's minor unit: all of the payment, or part of it. It is
taken from the funds due to you when the dispute opens, and returned if you win.

status.description:
`open` when the chargeback arrives; `under_review` while the operations team work the
case; then `won`, `lost` or `accepted`, each final. See [Disputes](https://docs.payments.finfactory.dev/merchant/guides/disputes/).

reason.description:
What kind of dispute it is, from the network's reason code. `fraud`: the cardholder says
they did not make the payment. `authorization`: the payment was not properly authorized.
`processing_error`: it was processed wrongly, such as charged twice, late or in the wrong
amount. `consumer_dispute`: the customer says what they paid for was not received, not as
described, or cancelled, or that a refund was not given. `other`: a code not in these.

network_reason_code.description: The card network's own reason code for the dispute, as it gave it.

case_reference.description:
The card network's reference for the case. Quote it when you talk to the operations team
about the dispute.

chargeback_cost.description:
What the card provider charges for the chargeback, in the dispute's currency and minor
unit, taken from the funds due to you with `amount`. `0` when it charges nothing.

admin_fee.description:
Your platform's own fee for handling a chargeback, if it sets one for the payment method,
taken with `amount`. Fixed when the dispute opens. `0` when there is none. It is not
returned when you win.

cost_returned.description:
What a won dispute gave back of `chargeback_cost`, in the same minor unit: returned to
you with `amount`. `0` until the dispute is `won` and the card provider returns its cost,
and `0` for one that is `lost` or `accepted`.

debited.description:
What came off your balance for the chargeback: `amount`, `chargeback_cost` and
`admin_fee` together. `0` when `charged_to` is `platform`. It stays the same once the
dispute is decided: what a win returns is `amount` and `cost_returned`. In test mode
nothing moves, but it says what would have.

charged_to.description:
Who bore the chargeback. `you`: it came off your balance, as `debited` says. `platform`:
the platform you take payments under bore it, and nothing came off your balance.

evidence_due_date.description:
The last day to respond with evidence, as a calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in your
platform's time zone. It may be moved while the dispute is worked. `null` until it is
known.

evidence_request.description: What the operations team asked you to send for the case, if they asked. `null` otherwise.
examples: Proof of delivery signed by the customer

created.description: When the dispute opened, as a Unix timestamp.

closed.description: When it was decided, as a Unix timestamp. `null` while it is `open` or `under_review`.

secret.description: The signing secret, `whsec_...`. Returned on create and rotate only.

id.description: Deduplicate on this; the same event may arrive more than once.

object.description: The object as the API shows it, as of this event.

Currency.description: A three-letter ISO 4217 code, in lower case.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

code.description: A stable name for this refusal. Branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: For the developer reading a log. May be reworded.

param.description: The field or parameter at fault, when there is one.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many objects to return, from 1 to 100.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
A value unique to this operation, such as your order number and attempt, of 1 to 255
characters. A retry with the same key and body is done at most once; see Idempotency.

RequestId.description: This request's id. Quote it when you contact support.
